text:
andrew: FYI — DeltaCo sales pinged about a Dedicated commit. They're proposing a 2.5M GPU-hour annual commit but want only a 3-week safety runway instead of our usual 8-week headroom. Is that safe from an ops perspective?

andrew: Their justification: predictable unit economics and they don’t want to pay for unused long headroom. They also expect big Q4 seasonality (x1.6).

sara: 3 weeks sounds thin. main risk is unplanned QPS spikes + rollout delays. if we miss capacity they expect failover to hosted model which has different cost/SLOs. :thinking_face:

sara: can we quantify outage probability with a 3-week runway vs 8-week? rough math helps negotiation.

leah: i'll run a Monte Carlo on their reported weekly profile. quick question: do we treat burst credits separate from commit for DeltaCo or allow burst on same pools?

andrew: sales prefers single pool (simpler for billing) but we could gate burst usage by a higher per-token price. need ops input on safety margin.

praveen: short answer: 3-week runway increases risk of forced throttles during correlated failures (region-level or infra upgrades). With their Q4 multiplier 1.6 and 95th-percentile bursts, probability of exceeding provision in a 2-week outage window is non-trivial.

praveen: rough numbers i pulled from similar customers:
```
baseline_weekly_gpu_hrs = 1400   # steady weeks
peak_95_weekly_gpu_hrs = 3200  # 95th percentile
q4_multiplier = 1.6
```

praveen: If we size for baseline * 1.0 + safety_runway_weeks * baseline, 3 weeks buys less headroom than a single severe peak week.

leah: Monte Carlo completed (quick, 10k sim). with their historical CV and Q4 multiplier:
- 3-week runway -> ~12% chance of >10% throttling days in the year
- 8-week runway -> ~2.3% chance of >10% throttling days

leah: so going to 3 weeks materially raises risk. :warning:

andrew: good data — can we translate that into expected SLA impact and extra cost if we fallback to hosted? sales needs $ delta.

praveen: ballpark: each throttled day -> ~0.6% revenue impact (customer-facing app), and fallback hosted run adds ~25% incremental cost on tokens served while capacity ramps. multiply by expected number of throttled days from sim.

andrew: can you prod the forecast into a simple table we can share with sales? they want: commit size, runway options (3w/5w/8w), expected throttled days, expected incremental hosted spend, and likely contract language (burst pricing).

leah: will do. delivering quick table in #calc-thread and attaching in the sales packet.

ops-bot: scheduled capacity-check job ran: current cluster utilization spike window next month shows 72% utilization expected in target region (west-us). Recommend pre-provision or reserve fallback region.

andrew: thanks. last q: policy-wise do we allow customers to opt for shorter runway if they accept explicit SLA credit terms? or do we force minimum 6 weeks?

praveen: ops prefers a minimum 6-week safety runway for new Dedicated commits unless customer buys explicit "rapid replenishment" add-on (guaranteed burst reserve + higher price). that add-on covers the operational risk.

andrew: ok — i'll propose 6-week default with an explicit commercial add-on to reduce runway to <=4 weeks. sales can present delta pricing and expected risk.

sara: suggest adding an automated alert: if observed 14-day rolling avg > 75% of provisioned commit, trigger a proactive capacity conversation. keeps things smooth. :thumbsup:

andrew: agreed. action items:
- leah: produce table for sales (commit vs runway vs risk/cost) -> due EOD today
- praveen: draft recommended ops language for contract add-on (rapid replenishment) -> EOD tomorrow
- infra: check multi-region fallback readiness for DeltaCo pools -> sync with eng-runtime

andrew: tagging @sara for alerting hooks and @ops-bot to run daily for DeltaCo until we close the deal.

sara: noted, i'll add the alert and a runbook snippet for the oncall.

praveen: also recommend one-time quarter-ahead warm-up (reserve X% for 2 weeks before Q4). extra cost but reduces throttle risk drastically.

andrew: perfect. thanks all.
